Examples.Title: Add labels to an inbox thread
Examples.Description: Applies one or more labels to the thread. Labels already on the thread stay on it. The response lists every label on the thread after the change. A label ID that is not a label of the inbox returns a 404 `Label not found.`, and nothing changes. A thread that does not exist in the inbox returns a 404 `Thread not found.`. To replace the labels of the thread, use the set thread labels endpoint.
Examples.Code:
### Add labels to an inbox thread
# @name inboxes/add-thread-labels
POST {{host}}/inboxes/{{inbox_id}}/threads/{{thread_id}}/labels
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

{
  "labels": [
    "7f9c1d2e-4a6b-4c3d-8e15-9b0a7c6d5e34"
  ]
}

## Responses
# 200
# Description: OK
# Content-Type: application/json

Examples.Title: Create a draft
Examples.Description: Creates an unsent draft on the inbox. Omit `thread_id` and `reply_to_email_id` for a draft that starts a new thread. Pass both together for a reply draft in an existing thread. A reply draft without `to` is addressed to the sender of the email it replies to, or to its Reply-To when set. For an email the inbox sent, it defaults to that email's `to` recipients. Send `to: []` to leave it empty. At least one of `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `text`, `html` or `attachments` must be non-empty. The combined recipients of `to`, `cc` and `bcc` cannot exceed 50. Attachments are stored on the draft, so each one needs `content`, `filename` and `content_type`. Returns 201 for a new draft. Only one unsent reply draft can target an email, so a reply draft request for an email that already has one returns 200 with the ID of the existing draft. An unknown `thread_id`, or a `reply_to_email_id` that is not in that thread, returns a 404. That request ignores every other field, except `attachments`, which replaces the attachments of the existing draft when sent. A reply draft created without `subject` stores an empty subject. When it is sent, it takes the thread subject, prefixed with `Re:` when it does not already start with it.
Examples.Code:
### Create a draft
# @name inboxes/create-draft
POST {{host}}/inboxes/{{inbox_id}}/drafts
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Idempotency-Key: {{Idempotency-Key}}
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

{
  "to": [
    "ada@example.org"
  ],
  "cc": "string",
  "bcc": "string",
  "subject": "Refund for order 1041",
  "html": "\u003Cp\u003ERefund issued for order 1041.\u003C/p\u003E",
  "text": "Refund issued for order 1041.",
  "attachments": [
    {
      "content": "aGVsbG8gZTJl",
      "filename": "receipt.pdf",
      "content_type": "application/pdf"
    }
  ],
  "thread_id": "4d8e2a1c-9b3f-4c6d-8a21-3e5f7c9c0d12",
  "reply_to_email_id": "5b1a9f47-2c8d-4e6f-9a03-1d2e3f4a5b60"
}

Examples.Title: Forward a thread email
Examples.Description: Forwards a message from the inbox address right away, with no stored draft. The original message is quoted under a forwarded-message banner, below the optional `html` or `text` note. The attachments of the original message are sent with the forward, together with any `attachments` you add. The request returns a 422 when they exceed 25 MB of `content` in total. An original attachment that was sent from a URL (`path`) cannot be forwarded, and the request returns a 422. The whole email, encoded, can be at most 40 MB, or the request returns a 422.

Examples.Title: Retrieve a list of drafts
Examples.Description: Returns the unsent drafts on the inbox, most recently updated first. The `after` and `before` cursors take a Draft ID from the current page, and only one of them can be passed. A cursor that is not a UUID, or both cursors together, return a 422. A cursor that is not an unsent draft on this inbox returns a 404.
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using Resend;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: Retrieve a list of inbox labels
Examples.Description: Returns every label on the inbox, oldest first. The list is not paginated.
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using Resend;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: Retrieve a list of thread emails
Examples.Description: Returns the messages of a thread, oldest first. Pass the `id` of the last message as `after` to get the next, newer page. Pass the `id` of the first message as `before` to get the previous, older page. Passing both `after` and `before`, or a cursor that is not a UUID, returns a 422. A cursor that is not a message of the thread returns a 404.
Examples.Code:
### Retrieve a list of thread emails
# @name inboxes/list-thread-emails
GET {{host}}/inboxes/{{inbox_id}}/threads/{{thread_id}}/emails?limit={{limit}}&after={{after}}&before={{before}}
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Accept: application/json

Examples.Title: Retrieve a list of inbox threads
Examples.Description: Returns the threads in an inbox, most recently active first. A thread is a conversation made up of one or more emails. The `after` and `before` cursors take a thread ID, and only one of them can be passed. A cursor that is not a UUID, such as a date, returns a 422 validation_error. A cursor thread that is not in the selected folders returns a 404. To find threads by text, sender, recipient, attachment, or date, use the search threads endpoint.
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using Resend;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: Remove a label from an inbox thread
Examples.Description: Takes one label off the thread. The label itself is kept, and stays on every other thread that carries it. To delete the label, use the remove inbox label endpoint. A label ID that is not a label of the inbox returns a 404 `Label not found.`. A thread that does not exist in the inbox returns a 404 `Thread not found.`.

Examples.Title: Reply to a thread email
Examples.Description: Sends a reply from the inbox address right away, with no stored draft. The `to` recipients come from the message you reply to. For a message the inbox received, the reply goes to its `Reply-To` addresses, or to its sender when it has no `Reply-To`. For a message the inbox sent, the reply goes to that message's `to` recipients. Set `reply_all` to also copy the other recipients of the message. The reply threads under the message through the `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers. When no recipient can be found for the reply, the request returns a 422. The whole email, encoded, can be at most 40 MB, or the request returns a 422.
Examples.Code:
### Reply to a thread email
# @name inboxes/reply-thread-email
POST {{host}}/inboxes/{{inbox_id}}/threads/{{thread_id}}/emails/{{email_id}}/reply
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Idempotency-Key: {{Idempotency-Key}}
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

"string"

Examples.Title: Search the threads of an inbox
Examples.Description: Finds threads by the text of their emails, who sent or received them, whether they have attachments, and their dates. Results are ordered by latest activity, newest first, and paginate like the list threads endpoint, so a cursor that is not a thread ID returns a 422. Search can be up to about a minute behind new emails. Different parameters combine, so a thread must match all of them. `folders`, `labels`, and `read` apply to the thread. `query`, `from`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `has_attachment`, `start_date`, and `end_date` must all match the same email in the thread. When any of these email filters is set, the matching email must itself be in one of `folders`. For `sent`, that means an email the inbox sent. When more than 10,000 threads match, search covers the 10,000 with the newest matching email.
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using Resend;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: Send a draft
Examples.Description: Sends the draft from the inbox address. A reply draft is sent in its thread. A draft without a thread starts a new thread. The draft must have at least one `to` recipient and `html` or `text`, or the request returns a 422. A standalone draft also needs a non-empty `subject`. A reply draft with an empty `subject` is sent with the thread subject, prefixed with `Re:` when it does not already start with it. A draft that was already sent returns a 409. The request body is optional and takes only `headers`. The whole email, encoded, can be at most 40 MB, or the request returns a 422.

Examples.Title: Set the labels of an inbox thread
Examples.Description: Replaces every label on the thread with the given labels, in one atomic change. Labels on the thread that are not in the list are taken off it. The labels themselves are kept. An empty array takes every label off the thread. The response lists every label on the thread after the change. A label ID that is not a label of the inbox returns a 404 `Label not found.`, and nothing changes. A thread that does not exist in the inbox returns a 404 `Thread not found.`.
Examples.Code:
### Set the labels of an inbox thread
# @name inboxes/set-thread-labels
PUT {{host}}/inboxes/{{inbox_id}}/threads/{{thread_id}}/labels
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

{
  "labels": [
    "7f9c1d2e-4a6b-4c3d-8e15-9b0a7c6d5e34"
  ]
}

Examples.Description: Marks a thread read or unread, or moves it to a folder. At least one of `read` or `folder` is required. To change the labels of a thread, use the add, set, and remove thread labels endpoints. This endpoint ignores the removed `add_label_ids` and `remove_label_ids` fields, so a body with only those fields returns a 422 validation_error.
